# CC0 / Public-Domain Art Reference Kit  
## Faces, Expressions, Fantasy Creatures & Monsters

A curated, quality-first set of CC0 and public-domain resources for drawing a wide range of human faces, expressions, and fantasy creature designs.

---

## How to use this kit

1. **Start with Duchenne** to understand the muscle mechanics behind an expression.
2. **Add a modern portrait reference** for age, likeness, lighting, and skin rendering.
3. **Translate the expression onto a creature** while preserving its emotional silhouette.
4. **Use historical monster art** to study exaggeration, horns, fangs, texture, and symbolic design.
5. **Use CC0 3D assets** when you need to rotate a form, test lighting, or understand volume.

---

## Core expression references

| Resource | Best for | License / status |
|---|---|---|
| [Duchenne — *Mécanisme de la physionomie humaine* (NLM)](https://collections.awsprod.nlm.nih.gov/catalog/nlm:nlmuid-60221710R-mvset) | The best historical source for isolating facial muscles and expressions: surprise, pain, fear, attention, smiling, and more. | Public Domain Mark |
| [Wellcome Collection — Duchenne facial-expression photographs](https://wellcomecollection.org/works/dm4eg9f4) | Clean, browsable plates of induced expressions; excellent for studying brow, eye, and mouth mechanics separately. | Public Domain Mark |
| [Wikimedia Commons — Facial expressions of humans](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Category:Facial_expressions_of_humans) | Broad pool of modern and historical expression references, drawings, and art-history examples. | Mixed — check each file |
| [Rawpixel CC0 search — portraits and faces](https://www.rawpixel.com/search/portrait%20human%20face%20cc0) | High-resolution public-domain portraits, expressive faces, vintage photography, and art references. | CC0 / Public Domain where labeled |

**Primary use:** Duchenne explains *how* an expression works; modern portrait references show *how it looks* under real lighting and anatomy.

---

## Face construction and diversity

- **Rawpixel portrait search** — Use for age range, ancestry/phenotype, head shape, lighting, and unusual face types. Search “portrait CC0,” “elderly portrait CC0,” or “expressive portrait public domain.”  
  <https://www.rawpixel.com/search/portrait%20human%20face%20cc0>

- **OpenGameArt CC0 Portraits** — Useful for stylized, game-facing face sets, avatar variation, and expression shorthand.  
  <https://opengameart.org/content/cc0-portraits>

- **Open Peeps** — CC0 hand-drawn modular people library with bodies, hairstyles, poses, clothing, and expressions. Best for cartoon, comic, and UI character design.  
  <https://www.openpeeps.com/>

### Build face range across four axes

- Age
- Ancestry / phenotype
- Head angle
- Emotional intensity

Duchenne covers emotional intensity exceptionally well; Rawpixel and Wikimedia are stronger for the other three.

## Fantasy creatures and monsters

| Resource | Best for | License / status |
|---|---|---|
| [Rawpixel — Public Domain Monster Images](https://www.rawpixel.com/search/public%20domain%20monster) | Historical dragons, demons, chimeras, harpies, mythological engravings, and expressive monster art. | Public Domain / CC0 where labeled |
| [OpenGameArt — CC0 creature collections](https://opengameart.org/content/cc0-resources) | Creature silhouettes, monster concepts, demon sketches, and game-ready assets. Quality varies; curate selectively. | CC0 on tagged assets |
| [OpenGameArt — 50+ Monsters Pack 3D](https://opengameart.org/content/50-monsters-pack-3d) | Broad CC0 3D monster library, useful for rotating forms and making 2D studies. | CC0 |
| [Poly Haven](https://polyhaven.com/) | Not creature art, but the best CC0 source for lighting, materials, HDRIs, and 3D assets for creature rendering. | CC0 |

### Creature-face method

- Use **animal anatomy** for plausibility.
- Use **public-domain monster art** for expressive exaggeration.
- Use **OpenGameArt concepts** for modern genre shapes and silhouettes.
- Change only one anatomical system at a time: eyes, jaw, skull, skin, or teeth.

---

## Recommended starter set

For a compact but powerful reference library:

1. **Duchenne via Wellcome / NLM** — expression mechanics  
2. **Rawpixel CC0 portraits** — human face diversity and realism  
3. **Rawpixel public-domain monsters** — fantasy visual language  
4. **OpenGameArt CC0 creature concepts** — modern creature design  
5. **Poly Haven** — lighting, materials, and 3D support  

---

## License notes

- **CC0** means “no rights reserved.” You may use, modify, redistribute, and commercialize the asset without attribution, though credit is courteous.
- **Public Domain Mark** means the institution believes copyright no longer applies. Generally safe, but confirm the individual item page.
- **Wikimedia Commons** hosts mixed licenses. The category page is not a license guarantee—check every image.
- For any resource with mixed licensing, filter explicitly for **CC0** or **Public Domain Mark** before downloading.
